item.title: The Corn Rake Witness | Post Mortem
item.description: "48 Hours" correspondents Anne-Marie Green and Erin Moriarty discuss the case of Todd Mullis, who was convicted of killing his wife, Amy Mullis, with a corn rake. They share Moriarty's exclusive interview with their son, Trysten, who says his father is innocent and is fighting to overturn his conviction. They also break down the scientific analysis by new defense experts who believe Amy's death was an accident.

item.title: Lady Gaga's family restaurant Joanne Trattoria celebrates singers on the rise
item.description: Joanne Trattoria empowers young singers to lift their voices. The cozy restuarant in New York City's Upper West Side is run by Joe and Cynthia Germanotta, the parents of Stefani Germanotta — also known as Lady Gaga.

item.title: 2 Americans die in suspected drowning incident in the Bahamas
item.description: Police said the Americans were part of a group swimming beyond an area marked with a warning sign cautioning against strong currents.

item.title: Exclusive discounts from CBS Mornings Deals
item.description: On this edition of CBS Deals, we show you items that could help improve your everyday lifestyle. Visit cbsdeals.com to take advantage of these exclusive deals today. CBS earns commissions on purchases made through cbsdeals.com.

item.title: Travelers stranded, flights canceled after ground stop. Here's what we know
item.description: More than 3,800 flights were canceled Saturday, according to flight tracking website FlightAware, while around 2,000 others were delayed.

item.title: U.S. loses measles elimination status as cases surge nationwide
item.description: The United States has lost its official measles elimination status for the first time in 26 years. Here's what to know.

item.title: Investigators probe cause of deadly NYC building collapse
item.description: New York City investigators are looking into whether anything criminal contributed to the deadly collapse of a building in Brooklyn.

item.title: New Orleans river cruise collision sounded like "tons of steel crunching," witness says
item.description: Shocking video shows the moment when a tanker and a paddlewheel river cruise collided in New Orleans. Luckily, no one died. Skyler Henry has more.

item.title: 3 oil tankers hit mines in Strait of Hormuz, Iran says
item.description: Fires had broken out on a total of three oil tankers that struck mines in the Strait of Hormuz overnight and into the morning, Iran's military said Saturday.

item.title: How Nvidia scandal, Anthropic IPO may impact your 401(k)
item.description: Nvidia's stock tumbled following a scandal involving former CEO Jensen Huang. Meanwhile, Anthropic prepares for its IPO. Kelly O'Grady explains what you should know.

item.title: Nvidia scandal exposes potential holes in U.S. national security
item.description: Jensen Huang is out as Nvidia's CEO after an extramarital affair with a suspected Chinese spy. Now members of President Trump's Cabinet are playing the blame game over restricted microchip exports to China.

item.title: Eye Opener: National ground stop lifted
item.description: A national ground stop caused a series of travel delays. Hundreds of "Rocky" fans gather to dress like Rocky Balboa for a Guinness World Record. All that and all that matters in today's Eye Opener.

item.title: Air travel chaos after national ground stop lifted
item.description: Thousands of travelers are still dealing with flight delays and cancellations after the FAA lifted a national ground stop order. The ground stop highlighted a worsening air traffic network crisis, former NTSB chair Robert Sumwalt explains.

item.title: Bomb found at industrial plant in Peoria, Illinois; rendered safe
item.description: Police said the device had been rendered safe but they are still searching the industrial area.

item.title: FAA lifts nationwide ground stop that disrupted thousands of flights
item.description: The rare nationwide ground stop lasted about five hours on Friday. An update to the network connecting the air traffic control system caused a reboot, crash and outage, sources told CBS News.

item.title: Alaska elects first Democratic governor since 1998
item.description: Jonathan Kreiss-Tomkins, also known as JKT, campaigned on issues including affordability and funding of public schools

item.title: Man in his 70s diagnosed with heart defect usually found in infancy
item.description: Carlos Perez's doctors didn't know why his heart was having trouble. Then a scan showed something they had never seen before.

item.title: From the archives: An artistic labor of love
item.description: Artist Mary Whyte is creating a record of those whose labors reflect a changing world. Correspondent Martha Teichner talked with Whyte about her watercolor portraits of men and women - a movie projectionist, a textile mill worker, a fisherman - that can become, Whyte says, "a person's resume of their life," in this "Sunday Morning" story that originally aired on Sept. 5, 2010.

item.title: Trump, Putin, Xi Jinping to meet in first trilateral of its kind
item.description: President Trump is looking to talk about reducing nuclear arsenals in the first formal trilateral between the leaders of U.S., China and Russia.

item.title: Microsoft says it "restored service" after major worldwide outage
item.description: A Microsoft outage involving services like Outlook and Teams impacted many users, companies and government services.

item.title: Passengers rescued after tanker hit river cruise in New Orleans
item.description: A tanker struck a river cruise ship on the Mississippi River near the Port of New Orleans Friday, partially submerging the passenger boat.

item.title: How "Banana Man" took a small Indiana town by storm
item.description: Banana Man began popping up around Linton, Indiana, a few months ago. Videos that also began circulating on social media appeared to show a boy biking all over town in a banana suit.

item.title: Nationwide ground stop lifted, Duffy calls for congressional funding to upgrade ATC system
item.description: The FAA on Friday night lifted a nationwide ground stop issued hours earlier over what DHS Secretary Markwayne Mullin called a telecommunications outage. Mullin and Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy took questions on the situation from the White House.

item.title: SpaceX launches first-of-its-kind Starship test flight
item.description: The SpaceX Super Heavy-Starship was designed from the ground up to be fully reusable in a bid to lower launch costs.

item.title: Lutnick agrees to testify as Bessent blames him for chip sales
item.description: Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has agreed to testify before the Senate Banking Committee on Dec. 10, according to a U.S. official.

item.title: Update to network connecting ATC system led to outage before ground stop, sources say
item.description: An update to the private communications network that connects America's air traffic control system caused the system to reboot, leading to a crash and a communications outage, multiple sources told CBS News. Lindsey Reiser anchors continuing coverage.

item.title: 11/13: CBS Evening News
item.description: Latest on FAA's national ground stop; No fatalities in New Orleans ship collision.

item.title: Never bought Nvidia stock? Its slide could still hit your 401(k).
item.description: Millions of Americans are exposed to Nvidia shares through their retirement plans. That's not as bad as it sounds (really!).

item.title: Family Dollar to pay $63M after FTC says it overcharged customers
item.description: The discount retailer failed to honor prices displayed on store shelves, on price tags and in ads, the FTC and multiple states alleged.

item.title: Inflation isn't going away. Here's what that means for interest rates.
item.description: As inflation seeps deeper into the U.S. economy, the Federal Reserve may have to step up the pace of rate hikes, according to Wall Street analysts.
